athena.architectures.mamba module

Mamba implementation.

class athena.architectures.mamba.AthenaMamba(cfg)[source]

Bases: Module

Sequence-to-scalar model for predicting value outputs from a FEN-token + action sequence.

The sequence is embedded, optionally given positional encodings, and fed through a stack of Mamba layers. A final LayerNorm and linear head produce logits.

Parameters:

cfg – Configuration object with attributes: - architecture.type: Must be “mamba”. - architecture.width: Model width. - architecture.depth: Number of Mamba layers. - architecture.d_state: Hidden state size inside each Mamba. - architecture.d_conv: Convolution width inside each Mamba. - architecture.expand: Channel expansion factor in Mamba feed-forward. - K, M: Same as in Transformer version (number of bins).

count_parameters() → int[source]

Counts the number of trainable parameters in the model.

Returns:

Number of trainable parameters.

Return type:

int

encode_win_prob(win_prob, mate, K=128, M=20) → ndarray[source]

Encodes the winning probability and checkmate status into a tensor.

Parameters:

  • win_prob (float) – Probability of winning, in [0, 1].

  • mate (int or str) – Mate index in [-M, M] or ‘#’ / ‘0’.

  • K (int, optional) – Number of win probability bins. Default is 128.

  • M (int, optional) – Number of checkmate bins. Default is 20.

Returns:

One-hot encoded tensor of shape (K + 2*M + 1,).

Return type:

np.ndarray

Forward pass of AthenaMamba.

Parameters:

  • action_idx (torch.LongTensor) – Tensor of action indices, shape (B,).

Returns:

Logits for value predictions, shape (B, K + 2*M + 1).

Return type:

torch.Tensor

class athena.architectures.mamba.MambaLayer(dim: int, d_state: int = 16, d_conv: int = 4, expand: int = 2, dropout: float = 0.1)[source]

Bases: Module

A single residual Mamba block that can replace a Transformer decoder layer.

Uses the Mamba SSM mixer for linear-time sequence mixing instead of attention. Applies pre-layer normalization and a residual connection.

torch.Tensor

athena.architectures.transformer module

Decoder-only transformer model with SwiGLU feedforward for action-value prediction.

This module implements the AthenaTransformer model, including: - SwiGLU feedforward layers - Decoder layers with post-norm attention - Embedding layers for tokens, actions, and positions

class athena.architectures.transformer.AthenaTransformer(cfg)[source]

Bases: Module

Decoder-only transformer for action-value prediction.

For state-value or behavioral cloning, omit the action token when building the sequence and change the output projection accordingly.

cfg – Configuration object containing model hyperparameters.

class athena.architectures.vit.AthenaViT(cfg)[source]

Bases: Module

Vision Transformer adapted for chess position evaluation.

Takes 8x8x28 input tensor and outputs win probability distribution.

count_parameters()[source]

Returns the number of parameters in the model.

encode_action_value(fen, move_uci, input_channels=24)[source]

Convert a FEN and move into an AlphaZero-style input tensor with move encoding.

Parameters:

  • fen (str) – The FEN string representing the chess position.

  • move_uci (str) – The UCI string representing the move to be made.

  • input_channels (int) – The number of input channels for the tensor.

Returns:

A 8x8xN tensor where:

  • Planes 0-17: Board state encoding (as before)

  • Plane 18: ‘From’ square of the move (1 where piece moves from)

  • Plane 19: ‘To’ square of the move (1 where piece moves to)

  • Plane 20: Promote to Queen (entire plane 1 if promotion)

  • Plane 21: Promote to Rook

  • Plane 22: Promote to Bishop

  • Plane 23: Promote to Knight

Return type:

np.ndarray

encode_win_prob(win_prob, mate, K=128, M=20)[source]

Encode win probability and mate information into a tensor with K + 2*M + 1 bins.

We need the extra bin for the move that checkmates the opponent. This extra bin isn’t shown on the negative side of the tensor, since a move that checkmates yourself is illegal. Bin structure: [-M1, …, -M20, win_prob_bins…, M20, …, M1, M0 (Move that checkmates opponent)]

Parameters:

  • win_prob (float) – Win probability in [0, 1].

  • mate (int) – Number of plies to mate. Positive = mate for, negative = mate against.

  • K (int) – Number of win probability bins.

  • M (int) – Number of mate bins on each side.

Returns:

One-hot encoded tensor of shape (K + 2*M,)

Return type:

np.ndarray

Forward function for the Vision Transformer.

Input shape: (batch_size, channels, height, width) Output shape: (batch_size, output_bins)
